reasons: Performance and accuracy numbers are unsupported by code or data in this packet.
Button inside link structure may confuse keyboard and screen reader users.

terms.meaning: The large opening area at the top of a home page, usually with a headline and main button.
The visible part of the browser window, used to decide when animations start.
A clickable item that takes the visitor to another page.
Short headline numbers meant to build trust quickly.

used_by: The / address, shown first to visitors

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the home page
sections.what: Loads links, animation, icons, the shared decorative icons, and the logo.
sections.why: Needed for the home page's links, animation, and branding.
sections.watch_out: Depends on the TechIcons and GokuLogo components, whose files are not in this packet.

sections.name: Home (part 1)
sections.title: Hero headline and main buttons
sections.what: Shows the large headline Custom AI Tools, Your Industry, a short paragraph, and two buttons: Build Custom Tool goes to the console and Browse Tools goes to the tools page.
sections.why: Likely reason: sends visitors to the main actions right away.
sections.watch_out: A button sits inside a link, which is not valid HTML and can confuse assistive tools.

sections.name: Home (part 2)
sections.title: Headline stats and entry animation
sections.what: Shows three stats: 2 to 4 week pilots, 6 AI tools, and 100 percent human verified. Each slides in with a short delay.
sections.why: Likely reason: quick credibility points for visitors.
sections.watch_out: The 6 AI tools count is typed by hand and is not tied to the tools page.

sections.name: Home (part 3)
sections.title: Preview card and floating badges
sections.what: Shows a fake terminal preview with four progress lines and two metrics, 14 day pilot duration and 97 percent accuracy. Two badges float up and down.
sections.why: Shows what the product looks like in use.
sections.watch_out: The 97 percent figure is typed in and not measured. Do not show it to customers without evidence.

sections.name: Home (part 4)
sections.title: Three-step process
sections.what: Three cards named Describe Challenge, Run Pilot, and Scale Results, each with an icon, step number, and short description.
sections.why: Explains how the product works in simple steps.
sections.watch_out: The 2 minute setup claim is text only and is not checked anywhere.

sections.name: Home (part 5)
sections.title: Capability cards
sections.what: Four cards in alternating lime and blue: Strategy Execution, Process Automation, Data and Analytics, and Risk and Governance. Each slides in from alternating sides.
sections.why: Likely reason: highlights the range of services with visual rhythm.
sections.watch_out: Any color value other than lime falls back to blue, so a typo changes the card's color quietly.

sections.name: Home (part 6)
sections.title: Closing call to action
sections.what: A headline saying Ship a pilot in 2 weeks, a short line describing the steps, and a Start Now button that goes to the console.
sections.why: Gives visitors one last push to start.
sections.watch_out: The 2 week promise is repeated across the site and is not backed by code.

sections.name: Home (part 7)
sections.title: Footer links and copyright
sections.what: Shows the logo, a short brand line, links to Tools, Frameworks, and Console, and a copyright line reading 2025.
sections.why: Gives quick navigation and a standard legal line.
sections.watch_out: The copyright year is typed by hand and is already out of date relative to the packet date of 2026.

summary: The home page, which introduces the product with a hero section, a three-step process, capability cards, a closing call to action, and a footer.
purpose: First impression for visitors. It explains what the product does and sends people to the console, tools, and frameworks pages.
why: Likely reason: marketing landing page. Reason not stated in the code beyond the sales content.
how: The page draws a hero with headline, buttons, and stats, then a card preview with floating badges, then three process steps, four capability cards, a closing call to action, and a footer. Animations run as sections appear on screen.
outputs: A marketing screen with links to other pages. No data is saved.
risks: Many claims such as 97 percent accuracy, 2 minute setup, and 6 AI tools are typed by hand and not measured. A button sits inside a link, which is not valid nesting.
debug: If a link fails, check the href value and the matching page file. If an animation does not start, check the viewport settings. Look for claims that need evidence before sharing.
